lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Equity securities
lines.why: Shares held for their return: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt (incl. current portion)
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans, current maturities included: financial.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: The difference between the 67.6% of days with buy-and-hold gains for Regulatory VaR back-testing and the 98.9% of days with trading, net interest and other revenue associated with Citi’s trading businesses, presented in the histogram of daily trading-related revenue, reflects, among other things, that a significant portion of Citi’s trading-related revenue is not generated from daily price movements on these positions and exposures, as well as differences in the portfolio composition of Regulatory VaR and Risk Management VaR.
Available-for-sale debt securities increased $20 billion, or 9%, driven by net purchases of foreign government securities, partially offset by net sales of U.S. Treasury securities.

Citi’s Ability to Return Capital to Common Shareholders Substantially Depends on Regulatory Capital Requirements, Including the Results of the FRB’s Stress Testing and CCAR Regimes, and Other Factors.
Citi’s ability to return capital also depends on a variety of other factors, including, but not limited to, the following:
Forecasts of future taxable earnings will depend upon various factors, including, among others, macroeconomic conditions.
Citi’s performance and the performance of its individual businesses largely depend on the talents and efforts of its highly qualified employees.
Citi’s ability to attract, retain and motivate employees depends on numerous factors, some of which are outside of Citi’s control.

Citi may also rely on AI models developed by third parties and be exposed to risks arising from their development and training methods, including potential inclusion of unauthorized material in the training data or limitations in their risk mitigation strategies, over which Citi may have limited visibility or control (see also the operational processes and systems risk factor below).
Citi develops its own software and relies on third-party applications and software, which are susceptible to vulnerability exploitations.
